error.message: At least one ID required for delete

tool.description: Delete entities by ID, or exact relationship triples. Use only for intentional removals after dependency checks. Do not use as a bulk cleanup shortcut. An entity authored in a Markdown or YAML source is not deleted directly: the call writes nothing and returns outcome plan_returned with a hash-bound deletionPlan and a nextActions entry holding the exact kb_apply_plan input ({plan, approvedPlanHash}); apply that unmodified, or repeat this call with approvedPlanHash = deletionPlan.planHash to apply the freshly computed plan in one step (a stale or different hash fails with DELETE_PLAN_HASH_MISMATCH and writes nothing). Authored requirements are never deleted: outcome supersession_required points to kb_upsert with a supersedes relationship. dryRun:true previews any delete and writes nothing. Side effects: mutates and saves KB and authored sources; skips entities with dependents; dryRun and plan_returned write nothing.

approvedPlanHash.description: With ids only: the deletionPlan.planHash a prior call returned; applied only while the hash still matches.

dryRun.description: Preview without writing: returns what a commit would delete and write.

ids.description: Entity IDs to delete after dependency checks.

relationships.description: Exact relationship triples to retract, including legacy shard records.

workspaceRoot.description: Optional absolute path of the workspace this call is about, such as your git worktree, when it is not the server's.

tool.name: kb_delete
